A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TC-Bench and WrongSelect study. The main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison despite repagination and v2's additional appendix.

before.justification: Tables 1–2 report original evaluations of test-generation methods and LLMs. The appendices include original scaling, stability, and failure analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains these empirical results and adds code-selection comparisons, rank distributions, and a Sliding Window case study with generated-test outcomes.

M1.justification: The binary failure representation, rank-sized basis, Jaccard objective, pre-filtering, and random-restart local search remain unchanged. Algorithm 1 is identical across versions.

E1.justification: Both retain the same competitive-programming coverage: 877 problems, 9,347 wrong C++ submissions, and 7,016 correct submissions. The added selection comparisons and Sliding Window analysis examine this benchmark; no additional dataset, domain, or language is introduced.

E2.justification: Section 4 and Figure 4 add two selection comparators, labeled TestCase-Eval and TCG, beyond the retained all-wrong-code comparison, now associated with TCGBench. The five main test-generation methods remain unchanged. Attribution is inconsistent: Section 4 cites Cao et al. for TestCase-Eval, whereas the bibliography identifies it as Yang et al.

E3.justification: The expanded 100-problem comparison introduces random selection of 20 codes and selection of five codes passing at least 60% of golden tests. Appendix C additionally evaluates 40 Claude-4-Thinking/LCB test cases. The main metrics and correct-code validation protocol remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 extends the inflation analysis with comparisons of selection strategies and their retained ranks. New Appendix C examines whether selected, excluded, and repeated codes correspond to distinct, composite, and equivalent faults, then analyzes missed faults in generated tests. Appendix A.5 also adds concrete failure illustrations.

E5.justification: The existing correct-code resampling stability analysis is retained. V2 introduces no new seed information, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The 40 generated cases in Appendix C are an evaluation sample, not repeated trials.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 1–2 remain unchanged, including Claude4/HT's 62.96% HackRate. Figure 4 adds selector-comparison results and rank distributions. Appendix C reports reducing 96 wrong codes to eight and excluding six of those eight using 40 generated tests. Appendix A.5 revises its failed graph-generation example from requiring a disconnected graph to a connected graph.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, optimization objective, and rank-based conditions are retained. Section 4 adds a rank-three matrix example and explains redundant columns, illustrating the existing rank-bound argument without introducing a new theorem, formal assumption, or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: rank-based benchmark construction, WrongSelect, TC-Bench, and substantial shortcomings in current test generators. The shortened abstract and added supporting analyses do not redefine these claims.

C2.justification: Section 4 adds explanations of random-sampling inflation, fixed-size selection's under-representation, and rank-based testing budgets. Appendix C introduces substantial interpretations connecting signatures to semantic faults and graded diagnostic capability. Its explanation of missed faults is internally problematic: C.4 describes queue-capacity failures, while C.1 shows sparse-table dimension errors for Basic WC6 and WC7.

D1.justification: Appendix C supplies annotated C++ listings and failure signatures for inspecting the case study. V2 removes the reproducibility statement containing two anonymous code links, while retaining the public code and dataset links in the abstract. Existing construction settings and implementation descriptions remain substantially unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds the B4 reference and a focused CodeT/B4 discussion distinguishing their solution-selection objectives from TC-Bench's rank-and-basis construction. Section 4 expands comparisons with prior benchmark strategies, while the existing literature survey is largely retained.

P1.justification: V2 condenses the abstract, expands Section 4, separates result-discussion paragraphs, corrects cross-references, and updates author and conference information. It appends the case study and an LLM-use statement, but retains the main section order and most existing prose.

P2.justification: Figure 4 becomes a four-panel display with additional comparators and rank distributions. V2 adds failure illustrations and extensive highlighted code panels, rearranges retained appendix plots, and redraws the cleaning example in English. Figure 4's revised caption incorrectly exchanges the descriptions of panels (a) and (b).

improvement.justification: The added selector comparisons and inspectable case examples address gaps in v1's empirical support. However, inconsistent baseline attribution makes the named comparisons ambiguous, and Appendix C.4's queue-capacity explanation conflicts with the sparse-table code in C.1, weakening its claimed diagnosis. These problems affect the principal new evidence, leaving the net quality benefit uncertain despite useful explanatory and presentation additions.
